related_questions.question: How much does it cost to live in a retirement community in Virginia?

related_questions.question: What is the 80/20 rule for 55 communities in Virginia?
related_questions.snippet: In the simplest terms, the 80/20 rule means that 80% of the occupied residences in a given community must be occupied by those 55 years of age and older. That means the other 20% may be eligible for occupancy by those younger than the target age demographic.
related_questions.title: Understanding The 80/20 Rule in Active Adult Communities - 55places

related_questions.question: How much do over 55 communities cost?
related_questions.snippet: Seniors-only apartments tend to be the least expensive option, with a median cost of about $1,475 per month. In some 55+ communities, single-family style homes or townhouses cost about $2,207 per month. Independent living communities provide apartment living, services, and amenities for about $3,145 per month.
related_questions.title: The Cost of Retirement Communities: Compare Your Options

related_questions.question: Is it cheaper to live in a 55- and older community?
related_questions.snippet: Higher Cost of Living Many benefits associated with active adult communities are excellent but come with a cost. HOA fees are often higher than typical neighborhoods, and some communities charge additional fees to cover amenities and services that come with a property.
